supported_judgments.finding: Untrusted search cannot extend owner constraints; standing delegation and an unregistered solver positive witness preserve permissionless usability.

OWS policy enforcement is not cryptographic attenuation when token and ciphertext permit secret recovery; design explicitly relocates enforcement or states trusted-signer assumptions. Owner-policy bypass is reported as access-model behavior, not a newly discovered exploit.
Authorization, facilitator verification, submission, finality, availability and recipient delivery remain distinct. A402 result-at-vault is correctly rejected as unconditional recipient delivery.
Unknown outcomes retain duties; retry and reconciliation preserve request identity and concurrent reservations; refund versus compensation is explicit and no global rollback is assumed.
ZK/MPC/TEE/PCD bind a common statement but retain different assumptions. Design makes no implemented compiler, federation, attestation or target proof claim.

caveats.point: Exact-byte decoding does not alone predict arbitrary state-dependent execution. The stated comparison with actual target effects must become an authenticated-state and execution-correspondence judgment, including fees and failed-stage effects.

MPLR031 rejects token possession as unrestricted signing authority under the proposed Moriarty capability policy; this should not be read as contradicting OWS owner-mode full access or preventing a principal from explicitly delegating full authority.

Current x402 supports multiple schemes. The design correctly avoids importing the older papers simplified per-request model into every current scheme. Specific pending/capture/void behavior belongs to pinned adapter profiles.

MPLR031–034 are supported as specialized refinements of authority, aggregate resources, staged settlement and replay identity; allocating IDs is parent-owned governance, not a claim that these are independent mathematical axioms.

evidence.coverage: Own source-grounded four-paper study and current proxy comparison.
Sibling source-verified claims reviewed; primary policy documentation independently reread.

limitations: No policy bypass executed, transactions sent, new tests run or cryptographic proof accepted.
